question: Do the retained Fr 8073 source views contain a text boundary that orders the photographs, and is the stanza order distinctive?
local_boundary: The bottom text of capture 2 provisionally ends Ex hac car-; the top text of capture 3 begins nis planta surgit virgo sancta. The combined phrase fits the same stanza of Lucis huius festa. These are images attributed by the existing manifest to the same catalogue object.
interpretation: The split word and surrounding text support the textual order capture 2 before capture 3, with immediate continuation conditional on the same occurrence and no missing material. The result is an intra-object text sequence, not a new cross-fragment join.
published_controls: AH 52 no.101 and a Cantus indexed Zutphen 6 f.246r inventory list the same six stanza openings in this order; Kelemen's published Tolnai breviary transcription presents a different order. These do not establish book identity or independent confirmation of the Swedish reading.
variant: Capture 3 provisionally reads Celo tam sublata mulier sancta ... soluat a reatu, while the AH 52 no.101 OCR base has Caelo iam sublata mulier beata ... purget a reatu. Earlier attestation, exact letters and distribution require further checking; no unique variant is asserted.
limits: Text selection and reading were reference-exposed and unreviewed. The catalogue claims one leaf, but the actual original side or quire mapping, photographic folding and composite/duplicate possibilities have not been independently resolved. The 1909 edition supplies prior art; no source-exemplar image was inspected.
next_test: Check the physical fold and document whether capture 2 and capture 3 are opposite original sides or other sections, compare the stanza and exact boundary against a corresponding passage on an existing Ant 49 candidate, and independently review the Latin reading.
